applicabilityBasis.summary: USDm, formerly cUSD, is marketed for dollar payments and transfers. Current V3 contracts mint/burn through reserve rebalancing and swaps against digital collateral. A legal issuer obligated to convert the token into a fixed amount of national currency or a bank deposit is not established. Protocol governance, reserve stewardship and infrastructure operators are identifiable, but operational control alone does not establish that statutory obligation. Payment intent and unresolved issuer/redemption evidence make applicability unclear.

genius.notes: USDm is a V3 reserve-backed stable asset, not a CDP merely because some other Mento currencies use CDPs. Payment marketing does not resolve GENIUS section 2(22)'s legal-issuer and fixed monetary-value redemption requirements. issuerEntity "Mento Protocol" is a factual protocol/control-domain descriptor, not an identified legal person or statutory GENIUS issuer. This preserves Mento-family issuer attribution without asserting that Mento Labs GmbH is the legal issuer. The reopened counsel workshop describes Labs as an infrastructure provider; MGP-19 describes Mento Labs GmbH as the reserve/oracle operator. Neither establishes a fixed monetary-value redemption obligation. issuerDomicile remains omitted because the legal token issuer is unresolved. Governance/admin powers, foundation stewardship and operator functions remain relevant and the protocol is not treated as immutable or exempt solely because a DAO participates. The 2024 workshop is issuer-side analysis, not an official GENIUS ruling; the August 2026 governance-transfer discussion is not evidence of execution. The opened reserve dashboard is first-party live disclosure, with no public 1:1 fiat issuer redemption policy or monthly independent reserve attestation established. No public token-specific GENIUS authorization, application, announced intent or registration was located. The full framework remains pre-effective; not-yet-restricted is a GENIUS timing description and does not establish permission under other US laws. MGP-18 separately describes existing migration-multisig control, so the older workshop claim of protocol immutability is not adopted as a current fact.

sourcesChecked: Official-domain web search on 2026-10-07: Mento, EURm, USDm, cEUR and cUSD combined with GENIUS, permitted payment stablecoin, enforcement and MiCA authorization across OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC, NCUA, Treasury, NYDFS and ESMA
negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No token-specific public GENIUS approval, state qualification, official application, foreign registration, announced GENIUS intent, or GENIUS enforcement action was located for EURm/USDm or the publicly described Mento operators in the opened official sources and targeted searches. The OCC directory covers national-bank applications, not all possible GENIUS filings. General rule proposals and unrelated licenses do not establish authorization. A legal issuer owing fixed monetary-value redemption remains unidentified in the reviewed disclosures; this finding records public evidence reviewed, not proof that no private filing or engagement exists.
